### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `findData (4 routes)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99c069652e82e4417fd4cd2f46ee83176f9bab98` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `012cd7e535f9291023fc6a48538bbf6f3d066662` — the merge of head `cbe0f85dd699d3116ea791b8b671fae1da81c294` into base `99c069652e82e4417fd4cd2f46ee83176f9bab98`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 012cd7e535f9291023fc6a48538bbf6f3d066662 && git checkout 012cd7e535f9291023fc6a48538bbf6f3d066662
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 99c069652e82e4417fd4cd2f46ee83176f9bab98 cbe0f85dd699d3116ea791b8b671fae1da81c294 && git checkout -B drift-repro 99c069652e82e4417fd4cd2f46ee83176f9bab98 && git merge --no-ff cbe0f85dd699d3116ea791b8b671fae1da81c294

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99c069652e82e4417fd4cd2f46ee83176f9bab98
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 99c069652e82e4417fd4cd2f46ee83176f9bab98` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:cloud#2 · os-zhuang · session_0123kRqqdpAJWYMgsgdAJX4G

Contract-review record · 2026-11-03T07:12Z · CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (fable, by an at-tier reviewer) on `a69e1db4` · Clause-② yes · **REQUEST-CHANGES** (one blocking item)

**Blocking.** `QUERY_PAGE_SIZE_EXCEEDED` is a synonym of the standard `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`.
- `errors.zod.ts:67` already declares `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` (400, "Query would return too many records").
- The ledger records ruling 6487532394 (#27277), which defines that member as "a caller-side limit, the request asked for more than a request may carry". A `limit` above the host's maximum page size is that case exactly. The member has no producer today, so this PR can be its first.
- Fix: answer the page-size refusal with `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` and drop `QUERY_PAGE_SIZE_EXCEEDED`. That halves the widening.
- `QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (offset plus rows walked, and the unpaged-analytics probe) is distinct and stays. Its ledger row should say in one line why it is not `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`, the way the `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP_EXCEEDED` row does.

**Holds as is.**
- (a) The widening is otherwise exact: nothing existing moved, and the changeset levels follow the rule.
- (b) Registration is consistent: the ledger, the catalog under 400, the count, and the status-conformance producers.
- (c) With no host configuration nothing clamps. Today's self-hosted behaviour is unchanged on every door, and tests pin it.
- (d) There is one rule, refuse and never clamp, and REST and both analytics doors share the planner.
- (e) The log line carries code, surface, object, rows and limit only.
- (f) Tests cover the refusal shape, the defaults, the probes and configuration faults.

**Non-blocking.** You can carry these in the same push:
- The limit reaches the wire only inside `message`. Lifting it into `details.limit` (`thread-http-error` mapping) would be the structured form.
- `data-api.mdx` says "neither request reaches the database". For a budget-only grouped read, the probe runs the aggregate and refuses afterwards, so tighten that sentence.

The seat re-reads on the next head. When it lands, the seat closes #29783 (the body says "Part of").

repo:cloud#2 · os-zhuang · session_0123kRqqdpAJWYMgsgdAJX4G

Contract re-read · 2026-11-03T07:47Z · head `23b7c161` · Clause-② yes · **ACCEPT**

- **The blocking item is resolved.** Page-size refusals now answer the standard `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` (400), which gets its first producer here and leaves the unpinned baseline (shrink-only). `QUERY_PAGE_SIZE_EXCEEDED` is gone from the ledger, the catalog, the docs, the changeset and the tests. The widening is now one member, `QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`. Its ledger row says why it is not `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`: the budget bounds how deep a query walks (offset plus page), so a page within the maximum can still be refused at a deep offset. The wire count is 57.
- **Non-blocking.** `data-api.mdx` now states that the budget probe read runs before refusing. Declining `details.limit` is accepted: `nestedRefusalEnvelope` forwards only the code, the message and the user message by rule, and changing that envelope is a separate shape decision outside this card.
- Everything that held at `a69e1db4` still holds: no default clamp, one refuse-never-clamp rule, logs carry counts only, tests cover it.

The merge state is `dirty`, so the dev thread will merge main into the branch. Automerge is armed, and the seat closes #29783 at landing.
